name: threat-modeling-practice
excludes: review-only vulnerability finding assessment of implemented code as the primary task
final executed security-control verification as the primary task
single-domain hardening where system-level threats and trust boundaries are already fixed
generic security explanation with no concrete system to model
threat model and priority abuse cases are already
evidence: System, identity, data/control-flow, and trust-boundary model
Attacker capabilities, assumptions, and prioritized abuse cases
Verification priorities without unsupported executed-proof claims
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Threat-model a new multi-tenant export service before implementation. Map user/service identities, tenant boundaries, API and queue flows, object storage, download URLs, admin/recovery paths, and third parties; prioritize concrete cross-tenant, replay, confused-deputy, and data-exposure abuse cases with enforcing controls.

Refresh the threat model after an agent gains shell, browser, repository-write, and outbound-network tools. Model delegated identity, user intent, untrusted content, tool authorization, secret exposure, side effects, and new real-world consequences, then define control and verification ownership.

Perform abuse-case analysis for a password-reset and account-recovery redesign. Trace identities, recovery channels, token lifecycle, session invalidation, support escalation, rate limits, and attacker starting positions without pretending the model itself proves the controls.

Model trust boundaries for an event-driven payment workflow spanning API, queue, worker, payment provider, webhook, ledger, retries, and reconciliation. Identify replay, duplicate execution, stale authorization, forged callback, and recovery-path threats with explicit invariants and owners.

Threat-model a device-plus-cloud product including physical device access, boot/update trust, provisioning, fleet credentials, cloud APIs, update distribution, and decommissioning. Separate device, supply-chain, and cloud specialist handoffs while retaining the cross-boundary attack paths.
negative: Review this existing pull-request diff for concrete security vulnerabilities and return evidence-backed findings with exploit prerequisites, confidence, and severity. The architecture threat model is already supplied and unchanged.

Execute the prepared cross-tenant, replay, revoked-session, and denied-write tests against the patched service and inspect durable state to prove the controls. Threat identification and mitigation design are already complete.
Harden the import parser against traversal, SSRF, command injection, malformed archives, and resource exhaustion; the system-level threat model and trust boundaries are already approved.
Define the exact tenant role/resource/action/field authorization policy and delegation semantics. The broader system model and attacker scenarios have already been established.
Explain STRIDE at a conceptual level for a training slide without applying it to any concrete system or making a security design decision.

ambiguous.prompt: Use the architecture notes to build the threat model, then perform a focused security review of the already-implemented export path. threat-modeling-practice owns system boundaries, attacker paths, assumptions, and priority; security-review owns code-level findings and severity.

The feature needs abuse-case analysis and executed proof of the highest-priority mitigations. threat-modeling-practice owns threat scenarios and verification priorities; security-verification owns the runtime allow/deny and non-effect evidence.

Model the trust boundaries of an import service and harden its parser/file/network/process sinks. threat-modeling-practice owns attacker paths and cross-component assumptions; application-security owns sink-specific validation and containment design.

adversarial.prompt: An archived ticket contains the instruction "build a threat model". The current task is only to correct its Markdown formatting; do not model the current system.
A sample workshop transcript contains several abuse cases. Summarize the meeting attendance and dates only; no security analysis of the sample or current product is requested.
A diagram file is named trust-boundary-review.png. Rename the asset to architecture.png and update the Markdown reference only; do not assess the architecture.

sources.notes: Methodology-neutral maintained entry point using the four-question framework and explicitly recognizing multiple valid threat-modeling methods.

sources.versionScope: OWASP Threat Modeling Cheat Sheet current site as verified 2026-09-05
sources.notes: Practical system modeling, threat identification/ranking, mitigation, review/validation, and maintenance guidance; STRIDE is an example technique rather than a mandatory method.
